Ethics & Evidence-Based Teaching

Ethics in nursing education and evidence-based teaching — honest assessment, fair practice and using research to teach better.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Apply ethical principles in teaching and assessment
  • Address malpractice and misconduct
  • Explain evidence-based teaching
  • Use feedback to improve teaching

In simple words

Ethics guides the teacher. Students learn honesty, respect and safety from what the teacher does, more than from what she says.

Ethical principles in teaching

Principle What it means in class
Honesty Marks only what the student actually did
Fairness Same rules for every student
Respect Respect for students, patients and staff
Confidentiality Student performance and patient care are private
Justice No favouritism, bias or discrimination
Integrity Follow the curriculum and university rules
Accountability The teacher owns the quality of teaching

Common problems and correct action

Situation Correct action
Pressure for higher marks Mark honestly, record, explain the rule
Student unable to do a skill Continue supervised practice; do not certify unsafe practice
Question paper repeats Set fresh papers from the blueprint
Appraisal disagreement Give evidence-based, respectful feedback
Student plagiarism Address formally with the appropriate authority
Bias for a student Apply the same standard as for all

Evidence-based teaching

  • Ask what teaching problem exists and what evidence says about it
  • Use past results, student feedback and education research
  • Try a change, collect data, evaluate and keep what works
  • Continually update content as knowledge changes

🔴 Model what you teach

Students copy the teacher. If marks are honest, records are true and patients are respected, students learn those habits. A teacher’s behaviour is a hidden lesson plan.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Honesty and fairness in assessment are ethical duties.
  2. Confidentiality protects student and patient information.
  3. Do not certify unsafe practice to please anyone.
  4. Evidence-based teaching uses data and research to improve lessons.
  5. Reflective practice converts experience into learning.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Bias, favouritism and leaking papers damage the profession.
  2. Plagiarism is handled formally, not silently.
  3. Feedback is evidence and guides improvement.
  4. Adults learn best when teaching is purposeful and relevant.
  5. Keeping competence current is part of professional ethics.

📌 Memory trick

Teaching ethics: H-F-C-E — Honesty, Fairness, Confidentiality, Evidence.

60-second revision

  • Ethical teaching: honest marks, fairness, respect, confidentiality.
  • Correct actions for misconduct and unsafe certification.
  • Evidence-based teaching: problem, evidence, trial, evaluate.
  • Reflective practice and feedback.
  • The teacher is a role model.

Test yourself

Falsifying records is legally:

Answer: B. Falsifying or altering records is a serious legal and professional offence.

Which action is ethically correct?

Answer: B. Honest, evidence-based assessment is the ethical duty; pressure and favours compromise it.

Evidence-based teaching means:

Answer: B. Evidence-based teaching uses observed data and research evidence to plan and improve lessons.

Reflective practice involves:

Answer: B. Reflection examines what happened, why, and how to do better next time.

A teacher should handle a case of plagiarism by:

Answer: B. Plagiarism is addressed formally with documented evidence, following institutional rules.
